beginner.summary: No cloud experience assumed. Participants learn the core AWS services for compute, storage, networking, databases, identity and monitoring, and deploy a small web application.
prerequisites: Basic computer and networking knowledge (IP address, DNS, web browser)
An AWS account or trainer-provided sandbox account with a budget alert
outcomes: Explain cloud computing, AWS global infrastructure and the shared responsibility model
Launch and secure EC2 instances, S3 buckets, RDS databases and a VPC
Control access with IAM users, groups, roles and policies
Deploy, monitor and cost-control a simple web application on AWS

objectives: Explain cloud service and deployment models

Secure and cost-protect a new AWS account

outcomes.outcome: Configure an AWS budget alert with an email notification triggered at a 10 USD threshold.

outcomes.assessed_by: Lab check: written Region choice rationale note

outcomes.outcome: Diagnose and resolve missing budget alert notification delivery issues.

subtopics: Navigating to the AWS Billing and Cost Management console

topics.best_practice: Configure budget notifications for both actual and forecasted spending thresholds.

subtopics: Enable MFA on the root account using an authenticator app

topics.best_practice: Secure the root account with MFA and configure budget controls immediately upon creating a new AWS account.

subtopics: Inspect AWS Budgets notification configurations and recipient details
Identify the incorrect email configuration or missing permissions
Fix the configuration, trigger a test notification, and verify receipt

seeded_failure.symptom: The participant triggers a test budget notification, but no alert email is delivered to the configured address.
seeded_failure.cause: The alert email address configured in AWS Budgets contained a typo, preventing email delivery.
seeded_failure.fix: Edit the AWS budget notification settings, correct the email address, save changes, and trigger a re-notification test.

quiz: What is the main financial difference between traditional on-premises infrastructure and cloud computing?

topics.failure_scenario: The developer user receives AccessDenied on aws s3 ls because an inline policy with an explicit Deny was attached to the user.

subtopics: Review of lab deliverables and AccessDenied results

seeded_failure.symptom: The developer user receives an AccessDenied error when attempting to run aws s3 ls, even though the Developers group has S3 read-only access.
seeded_failure.cause: An inline policy named BlockS3 with an explicit Deny for action s3:ListAllMyBuckets was attached directly to the developer user.
seeded_failure.fix: Delete the BlockS3 inline policy from the developer user account and retry the aws s3 ls command.
